svg.title: Iterator
svg.desc: Iterator. Walk a collection one element at a time without exposing how it is stored: an array, a tree or a stream that never ends. Step 1, The loop knows the storage: Three callers each page the API by hand, so switching it to cursor tokens edits all three loops. Step 2, An iterator hides it: orders.all() returns an iterator that keeps the cursor and a buffer; the loop never sees a page. Step 3, Lazy, one page at a time: One order per next(): page 1 serves three, the 4th fetches page 2, and break ends it before page 3. Step 4, Same loop, any structure: The same for…of walks an array, a tree in order and an endless generator cut short by take(5).

g.text: 3 · Lazy, one page at a time
3 · Lazy, one page at a time
Three callers each page the API by hand, so switching it to cursor tokens edits all three loops.
orders.all() returns an iterator that keeps the cursor and a buffer; the loop never sees a page.
One order per next(): page 1 serves three, the 4th fetches page 2, and break ends it before page 3.
The same for…of walks an array, a tree in order and an endless generator cut short by take(5).
The API moves from page numbers to cursor tokens:
no page number to count up, no hasMore flag
a new iterator on every call
for…of calls it for a new iterator
no page, no cursor, no hasMore in this loop
async generator · runs on next(), not on all()
for…of asks the source for an iterator,
then calls next() until done is true
Paging lives in every caller: one API change means three loops to edit
Cursor tokens now mean one edit, in allOrders(): no caller changes
Stripe's Node SDK pages list calls the same way, under for await
Lazy: 4 orders cost 2 requests, not 3; page 3 is never fetched
Iterable and Iterator, the enhanced for (T x : xs)
IEnumerable<T>, foreach, iterator methods with yield return
forEach(fn) runs the loop for you, so no break
